image_description: A museum display of a Triceratops fossil skeleton. The image shows the articulated bones, including the skull with three horns and large frill, the ribcage, spine, and limb bones, mounted on a rocky base against a dark background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skeletal structure clearly displays the characteristic three-horn arrangement: two large brow horns and one smaller nasal horn.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image depicts a fossilized skeleton. The beak described in the taxonomy is a keratinous soft-tissue structure which does not preserve in fossils and is therefore absent from the image.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skeletal mount shows four sturdy, column-like limbs supporting the body mass, consistent with a quadrupedal stance.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The large, shield-like bone structure at the back of the skull is clearly visible and dominates the head profile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears as a solid bony plate with visible texture and marginal osteoderms (bumps) along the edge, matching the skeletal description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This checkpoint refers to skin/integument. As this is a clean skeletal mount without skin impressions or mummified remains, this feature is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skeletal articulation shows the front legs are structurally shorter than the rear legs, resulting in the characteristic downward slope of the spine towards the head.
The caudal vertebrae are visible and appear relatively short and thick compared to other dinosaur families, consistent with ceratopsian anatomy.

To verify the 3D coherence of the complex overlapping bones and ensure no 'melting' or spatial errors typical of AI generation.
To assess lighting consistency, shadow casting, and texture realism of the bone material.

focus_areas: Skeletal anatomical correctness (horn count, frill shape)
